findings.title: Preserve the original contrast of embedded-reply links
findings.body: The light-theme branch for `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` changes the existing lightness adjustment from 30% to 70%. For example, with a #333 primary on a white background, these small links change from #707070 to #c2c2c2, reducing contrast from about 5:1 to 1.8:1 and making them difficult to read. Preserve the original 30% light-theme value and use the corresponding secondary-based 70% value for dark themes.

findings.title: Keep the original light-theme value for topic-map headings
findings.body: The `.topic-map h3` conversion also changes the light-theme adjustment from 20% to 50%, rather than only adding dark-theme handling. With a #333 primary, this changes the heading from #5c5c5c to #999999 on the light topic-map background. Since these headings are only 1em, the reduced contrast makes them substantially harder to read. Retain 20% for the light branch and use 80% for the secondary-based dark branch, as the desktop topic-map heading does.

findings.title: Avoid reducing group-member name contrast in light themes
findings.body: The light-theme branch for `.group-member-info .name` changes the previous adjustment from 30% to 50%. On the user-stream item's white background, a #333 primary therefore produces #999999 instead of #707070, dropping normal-sized member-name text from roughly 5:1 contrast to 2.8:1. The same regression appears in `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497`. Preserve the existing 30% light-theme value in both bundles and use the complementary secondary-based 70% adjustment for dark themes.
